svg.aria-label: Slopegraph of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index scores before and after the v4.1.1 patch released August 6 2026. The left column shows v4.1 scores carried through the August 8 brief; the right column shows v4.1.1 scores now published. Claude Opus 5 rises from 61 to about 63 and remains number one. Claude Fable 5 rises from 60 to about 62. GPT-5.6 Sol rises from 59 to about 60. Kimi K3 moves from 57 to about 58. Meta's Muse Spark 1.2 makes the single largest move, rising 2.7 points from 54 to 57, so its right-hand endpoint lands exactly where Kimi K3 sat before the patch. Artificial Analysis states most models moved less than a point and only Muse Spark 1.2 moved materially, so the roughly two-point lift at the top is finer rounding and snapshot noise rather than a capability jump. The ordering of the leaderboard is unchanged and no new model and no price cut occurred.
svg.title: The ruler moved, not the market — Index v4.1.1 (Aug 6) re-numbers the board upward, but the only material move is Muse Spark 1.2 (+2.7 → 57); order unchanged, no new frontier model, no price cut
svg.text: The ruler moved, not the market — Intelligence Index v4.1.1 re-numbers the board
AA Intelligence Index before (v4.1) vs after (v4.1.1, patched Aug 6). Grader upgrade + τ³-Banking v1.0.1 lifted absolute scores; AA says every model moved <1 pt except Muse Spark 1.2 (+2.7).
Muse Spark 1.2 · 57 (+2.7, the only real move)
lands exactly where Kimi K3 sat pre-patch (57)
v4.1.1 (Aug 6) is a PATCH, not a new benchmark set: it upgrades grader models (HLE, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience now graded by GPT-5.6 Luna medium, replacing GPT-4o / Qwen3-235B / Gemini 3 Flash) and
brings τ³-Banking to v1.0.1. AA: “most models move <1 pt… largest increase Muse Spark 1.2 +2.7… the same models hold the top.” So the ~+2 at the ceiling is mostly finer rounding, not capability.

The Aug-08 brief flagged Muse Spark as “54 (launch) vs 57 (one AA page)” and left it unreconciled — the 57 is simply the v4.1.1 number. Absolute v4.1.1 figures for the top vary by mirror (Opus 5 shown as 63.1).
What did NOT change this window: no new model (Aug 6–9), no flagship price cut, ordering intact, Opus 5 still #1. The number on the ceiling rose; the market underneath it did not move.
